m96_sui_col.notes: 0-0 through 90' and full 120' (AET) -- lowest 90-min combined xG of the tournament (0.7). Colombia dominated process throughout (xG 1.03 vs SUI 0.35; shots 15-7; corners 7-3) but could not convert: Lucumi header off the crossbar (~100', ET) and Campaz badly missed an open one-on-one chance after a Xhaka error (115'-116', the single biggest chance of the match). Switzerland won 4-3 on penalties (Colombia shot first): COL scored Quintero, Campaz, Diaz, missed Sanchez (crossbar) and Cucho Hernandez (saved by Kobel); SUI scored Xhaka, Amdouni, Itten, R.Vargas (winner, sent Vargas the wrong way), missed Akanji (admitted post-match he second-guessed his placement). Switzerland's first-ever WC shootout win (lost their only prior one, 2006 vs Ukraine); first Swiss WC quarterfinal since 1954. Team-news theses check: Luis Suarez started for injured Cordoba as expected (played 82', booked, subbed for Cucho who then missed his kick); James Rodriguez started and played a clean 66' with no visible illness recurrence (subbed for Quintero in what read as tactical, not forced) -- the illness risk resolved as the mild case, not the risk case, yet Colombia still lost; a previously unflagged injury (Johan Manzambi, out with a training knee injury) emerged that the pre-lock team-news sweep had not captured -- a genuine gap, not a contradiction. Net: the concrete rest/travel/injury edge Switzerland's J-instrument leaned on did NOT need to resolve in Switzerland's favor to produce a Switzerland win -- Colombia's doubts mostly resolved in Colombia's own favor and they still out-chanced Switzerland heavily, but lost anyway via shootout variance, not via the process edge the pre-match thesis identified. Switzerland advance to QF vs Argentina (Kansas City, 7/11). Sources: FIFA match centre, ESPN, FOX Sports box score, Opta Analyst, France24, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, ColombiaOne, cross-verified 2026-07-08.

m103_fra_eng.notes: England 6-4 France in 90' (bronze final, Miami; no ET needed). 10 goals -- first WC match with 10+ since Hungary 10-1 El Salvador (1982); England's best WC finish in 60 years. HT 0-4: Rice 3' (long-range curler), Konsa 18' (header), Saka 37' + 45+1'. 2H France rally: Mbappe 48', Barcola 54' (Mbappe assist, sub), Mbappe 66' -- reported by Olympics.com as making him all-time WC career top scorer, and taking him to 10 tournament goals (Golden Boot over Messi's 8, settled since Messi did not score in the final); Saka pen 87' (hat trick, 4th England men's WC hat-trick scorer); Dembele 90+6' (sub); Bellingham 90+8' (sub). xG: England 3.05 vs France 2.80 (Opta Analyst/xGscore -- highest combined xG of the tournament, 5.7); shots 19-19, SoT 11-9 England; possession 54-46 England. 1H England dominant (shots 11-5, SoT 7-2); 2H France dominant (xG 2.29-1.65, shots 14-8) -- process read: England's first-half blitz was real process advantage vs a flat, heavily-rotated France; France's 2H surge was real too but chasing from 0-4. LINEUPS/ROTATION (action-tree adjudication, counted vs each side's semifinal XI): France XI Maignan; Gusto, Konate, Lacroix, T.Hernandez; Rabiot, Zaire-Emery; Olise, Cherki, Doue; Mbappe = 7 changes from semi XI (Kounde/Upamecano/Saliba/Digne/Tchouameni/Dembele/Barcola out), 6 counted per pre-registered rule excluding Saliba. England XI D.Henderson; Quansah, Guehi, Konsa, Spence; Rice; Saka, Eze, Rogers, Rashford; Toney = 7 changes (Pickford/James/Stones/Anderson/Bellingham/Gordon/Kane out). England rotated MORE than France -- the 07-16 late-news reversal (England rotating harder, Kane to bench) materialized exactly; the locked J's asymmetric-rotation premise (France rotates, England near-full) was factually wrong by kickoff, as pre-flagged in the verdict's own 'where I might be wrong' item 1. T-75 ACTION TREE (pre-registered dead levels; NO session was present at T-75, so per the m91 rule these are recorded, not executed, and not retroactively claimed): triggered = Kane not in XI (+4 FRA), England changes >= France changes (+6 FRA), D.Henderson starts (+2 FRA); not triggered = Bellingham suspension (played as sub, never charged), Mbappe absent (started), Risser (Maignan started), FRA-ENG changes >=5 (6-7 = -1). Counterfactual net +12 France-ward would have made J's score WORSE on this outcome -- the tree pointed the wrong way this match. CONDITIONAL PAPER TICKET (from edge-hunt critique): required Kane+Bellingham+Rice all starting -- FAILED (Kane and Bellingham both benched), so no bet fired, correctly per its own registered conditions. Honest counterfactual both ways: England ML closed 4.57 (price condition >=3.85 held) and England won -- but the ticket's thesis was 'England full-strength value', and England won via exactly the opposite configuration (B-XI), so the ticket missing is premise-discipline working, not bad luck. The other registered candidate, BTTS No at FanDuel +210 (never taken -- price could not be mechanically verified), LOST at 54' (both teams scored) -- the price-verification rule saved 1u. Yamal started and was fine (first chance at 5', rated 7/10) -- the J-runner trial factor built on his fitness doubt resolved to nothing, exactly its own registered invalidation line. Enzo Fernandez sent off in 90'+ stoppage (second yellow, foul on Cubarsi), so Argentina played all of ET with 10 men -- confound for any ET-layer mechanism claims. EDGE-HUNT HONESTY RECORD: the strongest MARGINAL candidate (draw @3.02, from the 22-final 54.5% level-at-90 base rate) HIT -- 0-0 at 90'. It was correctly-per-rules not bet (MARGINAL, not REAL_EDGE; correlated cluster). Paired with m103's BTTS No candidate losing, the two registered-but-unbet candidates went exactly 1-1 -- n=2, no conclusion, recorded so the rules' filtering cost/benefit stays visible. MARKET: Pinnacle lock-time 2.34/3.02/3.63 -> closing 2.31/3.06/3.74, essentially stable; the market's extra Spain-lean vs M/J was directionally vindicated by process and outcome, but on the 90' vector the draw outcome scores M=J at parity-or-better vs the closing line (see score.py). The judgment layer's much stronger Spain lean (43.9/27.7/28.4) was process-vindicated (xG 1.94-0.20) but RPS-punished on the 90' draw -- the m91 settle language applies verbatim: the ledger goes to M/J, the reasoning goes to the judgment layer ('process advantage' vs 'finishing variance': Spain needed 106 minutes to convert total dominance).
